name: Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500)

b.x: Does combining BPC-157 and TB-500 actually produce better healing than either peptide alone? Thousands of community reports say yes. The first controlled animal test, in rats, found no added benefit. The Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500, also called the healing stack) is a pre-mixed 10 mg vial containing 5 mg of each component. BPC-157 is a 15-amino acid fragment of body protection compound, a protein found in human gastric juice. TB-500 is a synthetic 7-amino acid fragment (Ac-LKKTETQ) of thymosin beta-4, a 43-amino acid protein involved in cell migration. The two peptides work through different but complementary mechanisms. BPC-157 upregulates VEGFR2 and FGFR1 receptors at the injury site, promotes angiogenesis, and modulates the nitric oxide system. TB-500 is tied to G-actin binding, angiogenesis and cell migration, mostly from rat and cell studies of full-length thymosin beta-4 [5]. You don't need to inject TB-500 near the injury; it distributes body-wide. One retrospective chart review followed 16 knee pain patients (Lee and Padgett 2021) [7]. Only 4 received BPC-157 with thymosin beta-4, and 3 of them reported significant relief; 11 of 12 on BPC-157 alone did. A 2026 rat Achilles study (n=32) [6] found the pair no better than either peptide alone; TB-500 alone gave the clearest gains. Beyond that, evidence comes from the individual components: over 180 published BPC-157 papers (35 of 36 studies meeting systematic review criteria were preclinical per Vasireddi et al.) [2]. For TB-500, the closest human data comes from two phase 1 safety trials of its parent protein, full-length thymosin beta-4: Ruff 2010 [8] and Wang 2021 [3]. Community evidence is strong. Tens of thousands of user reports across r/Peptides, ExcelMale, and Longecity consistently describe accelerated soft tissue healing within 2 to 4 weeks. The Wolverine Stack is considered the gold standard healing combination. FDA's Category 2 page lists both as nominated for compounding, then withdrawn by their nominators. Neither is on the 503A bulks list, so U.S. pharmacies cannot compound them today.

Two repair systems working different angles from one syringe. BPC-157 acts at the injury site. It upregulates growth factor receptors VEGFR2 and FGFR1, triggering local angiogenesis. A 2025 review ties that angiogenesis to nitric oxide signaling through the Akt-eNOS axis [1]. In rats, Sikiric and colleagues linked its stomach-lining protection to adrenergic and dopamine systems [4]. TB-500 operates systemically. Its core mechanism is actin sequestration. By binding monomeric G-actin, TB-500 regulates cytoskeletal dynamics that control how quickly cells migrate to injury sites. Much of this comes from full-length thymosin beta-4, the parent protein. Malinda and colleagues found it raised reepithelialization 42% at day 4 and up to 61% at day 7 in rats [5]. Treated rat wounds also showed more collagen deposition and angiogenesis. It inhibits myofibroblast differentiation, which decreases fibrosis and scar tissue formation. The combination rationale is complementary rather than redundant. BPC-157 handles precision repair at the injection site; TB-500 sends repair signals body-wide regardless of where you inject. That rationale has had one direct test so far. In a 2026 rat Achilles study [6], the pair did no better than either peptide alone. No human pharmacokinetic study exists for the blend.
Wolverine Stack benefits center on tissue repair, pain reduction, and recovery acceleration.
Accelerated soft tissue healing in two to four weeks. Community consensus across thousands of user reports is remarkably consistent on this timeline for tendons, ligaments, and muscle tears.

Acute injury pain reduction within one to two weeks. Users frequently report meaningful pain relief before structural healing is complete, attributed to BPC-157 nitric oxide modulation and TB-500 cytokine suppression.
Post-surgical recovery support. The advanced protocol runs 1,000 mcg a day, split into two injections. Athletes and surgical patients use it for a faster return to function, per community reports.
Convenience of a single injection. The pre-mixed 1:1 blend eliminates the need to reconstitute and inject two separate vials.
Chronic tendinopathy response after four to six weeks. Repetitive strain injuries and long-standing tendon issues represent a slower but commonly reported response window.

Complementary local plus systemic coverage. BPC-157 targets the injury site through angiogenesis and VEGFR2 upregulation while TB-500 drives repair signals systemically through actin sequestration, cell migration, and angiogenesis. Those findings come from rats given full-length thymosin beta-4 [5]. Users consistently perceive the combination as superior to either peptide alone, though the one controlled rat study [6] found no added benefit.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 14 key studies · Research only
No published RCT or clinical trial specifically tests the BPC-157 + TB-500 combination as a pre-mixed formulation.
Dosing studied: 500–1,000 mcg/day total from pre-mixed vial (250–500 mcg each component); extrapolated from individual component animal data: no human dose-finding data for the combination

One retrospective chart review (Lee & Padgett 2021, n=16 knee pain patients) [7] gave 4 patients BPC-157 + thymosin beta-4; 3 of 4 reported significant pain relief: the only published human data on the combination. Individual component science is largely preclinical: over 180 papers on BPC-157 (35 of 36 meeting systematic review inclusion were preclinical; Vasireddi et al.) [2]. TB-500 itself has no published human study; two phase 1 trials, Ruff 2010 [8] and Wang 2021 [3], tested full-length thymosin beta-4. The combined Wolverine Stack has no dedicated human trial. Mechanistic rationale for pairing them: BPC-157 acts locally (VEGFR2/FGFR1 upregulation, angiogenesis, nitric oxide modulation) while TB-500 acts systemically (actin sequestration, cell migration, VEGF upregulation). The first controlled animal test of the pair (rat Achilles tendon, n=32) [6] found the combination conferred no additional benefit over either agent alone. TB-500 alone improved load to failure and histology scores; BPC-157 alone did not reach significance.
Key Study

Lee & Padgett 2021 (PMID 34324435; retrospective, n=16, knee pain): 4 received BPC-157 with thymosin beta-4 and 3 of 4 reported significant relief; 11 of 12 on BPC-157 alone did. Only published human data combining the two.
Limitations

No dedicated RCT. Only one retrospective human report includes the combination (4 patients, PMID 34324435). All other evidence is animal-based. No human dose-finding or PK study for the blend. Ratio locked at 1:1 in pre-mixed vials prevents independent component titration. Combination angiogenic safety (pro-tumor vascularization risk) has not been evaluated in humans.
Community Experience
Strong community consensus.

Community dosing: 500 mcg/day total (250 mcg each component) for maintenance; up to 1,000 mcg/day during loading. Some advanced users run TB-500 component separately at higher doses alongside BPC-157.

The Wolverine Stack is one of the most established peptide combinations. Tens of thousands of users report consistent outcomes. Protocol agreement is high across r/Peptides, ExcelMale, and practitioner guides. Considered the gold standard healing stack.
What users report (7)
Accelerated soft tissue healing (tendons, ligaments, muscle tears): most users report meaningful improvement in 2–4 weeks
Acute injury pain reduction within 1–2 weeks
Improved flexibility and range of motion around injured areas
Post-surgical recovery acceleration
Convenience: one injection covers both peptides
Combination perceived as superior to either component alone
Chronic tendinopathy and repetitive strain injuries often respond after 4–6 weeks
Common issues (8)
Nausea: most common complaint, attributed to BPC-157 gastric motility effects; worse at higher doses
Headaches during loading phase: attributed to vasodilation
"Peptide flu" in weeks 1–2: malaise, chills, transient fatigue; usually resolves
Injection site reactions: redness, lumps; often due to BAC water pH or benzyl alcohol, not the peptide
Heart palpitations: transient, most common in first few days
Anxiety or panic attacks in a subset of users (BPC-157 serotonin/dopamine modulation)
Pre-mixed ratio cannot be adjusted: users who need higher TB-500 dosing must supplement with separate TB-500 vials
Zero effect in some users: frequently attributed to counterfeit or degraded product

Science supports both individual components via preclinical evidence and one retrospective human combination report. Community protocol is mechanistically coherent with published science. Divergence exists on: (1) optimal dosing: community uses fixed 1:1 ratio from pre-mixed vial while science would support independent component titration; (2) loading structure: community adds TB-500-style loading to a daily BPC-157 protocol; (3) confidence ceiling: community treats this as well-established while evidence is still primarily animal-based.

Community Community figures. No study has given the blend to people, FDA found no human data for TB-500 (July 2026 briefing), and the rat doses (PMID 42542926) do not convert. 1,000 mcg a day total is the community ceiling [Source](https://www.fda.gov/media/193349/download)

The dosing math on a 10 mg pre-mixed vial (5 mg BPC-157 + 5 mg TB-500) reconstituted with 2 mL bacteriostatic water: 5,000 mcg/mL total (2,500 mcg/mL each component). On a U-100 insulin syringe: 5 units = 250 mcg total, 10 units = 500 mcg total, 20 units = 1,000 mcg total. Start at the beginner dose (500 mcg/day, which is 10 units). Most people tolerate it without issues. If nausea hits, drop to 5 units for a few days and work back up. Inject as close to the injury as you can safely reach subcutaneously. For deeper structures like Achilles or rotator cuff, inject into subcutaneous tissue directly above. BPC-157 benefits from proximity; TB-500 goes everywhere regardless. One thing beginners miss: product quality matters more with blends. Require LC-MS/MS confirmation that both BPC-157 (MW 1419.5 Da) and TB-500 (MW 889.0 Da) are present at correct masses. HPLC alone can't distinguish closely related impurities in peptide blends.
Cycling Protocol
Loading phase: full dose daily for 4-6 weeks. Then maintenance: half dose every other day. The TB-500 component benefits from a loading protocol.
Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500) Continuous

Both components individually are cycled 6 weeks on / 2 weeks off by community consensus. The rationale is: (1) TB-500 loading structure (higher dose for 4–6 weeks, then maintenance or rest) follows a standard loading protocol for peptides with systemic accumulation; (2) BPC-157 theoretical receptor desensitization: no formal data but consistent with peptide receptor downregulation principles; (3) safety monitoring: the 2-week off period allows assessment of any adverse effects before re-loading; (4) no published human safety data exists for TB-500 at any duration, and none for BPC-157 beyond a few weeks. The combined cycle follows whichever component has the more conservative cycling requirement.
Diminishing healing response despite continued dosing (suggests desensitization or resolved injury)
Persistent anxiety, mood changes, or palpitations beyond week 3 (suggests CNS sensitization)
New or worsening nausea after week 2 (expected in week 1 only)
Injection site reactions that are not resolving with site rotation

b.h: Reconstitute the 10 mg vial with 2 mL bacteriostatic water
b.x: Aim the stream along the glass wall. Do not shake. Swirl gently until dissolved (2 to 3 minutes). This gives you 5,000 mcg/mL total.

Draw your dose with a U-100 insulin syringe (29 to 31 gauge). Beginner: 10 units = 500 mcg total (250 mcg each component). Moderate: 20 units = 1,000 mcg total, once a day. Aggressive: the same 20 units once a day, because 1,000 mcg a day is the community ceiling; the post-op protocol splits it into two 10-unit draws. No published source sets a dose for the blend; these are community figures.

b.h: Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab
b.x: Abdomen (two inches from navel), thigh, or subcutaneous tissue directly above the injury. BPC-157 works best locally.
Insert the needle at a 45-degree angle. Push the plunger slowly. Release the skin, withdraw the needle, apply light pressure.
If injecting near an injury, alternate between two spots on opposite sides of the affected area.

b.h: Standard timing is morning before activity
b.x: For the twice-daily advanced protocol, space injections 8 to 12 hours apart.
Store the reconstituted vial in the refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees C. Use within 3 to 4 weeks. Never freeze reconstituted solution.
Alternative Routes
Oral (BPC-157 component only)

BPC-157 alone is acid-stable and used orally for gut healing at 500 mcg. However, the TB-500 component has no established oral bioavailability: it would be degraded in the GI tract. For oral gut healing, standalone BPC-157 is required; the pre-mixed vial should not be used orally.
If the goal is gut healing specifically, use standalone BPC-157 oral. The Wolverine Stack pre-mixed vial is subcutaneous only.
Intramuscular (IM)
Same dose, different absorption kinetics. BPC-157 benefits from proximity to injury (SQ preferred). TB-500 is fully systemic regardless of route.
IM injection acceptable if preferred. Glute or deltoid common sites. SQ is preferred for the blend because BPC-157 local healing effect is preserved.
Works With
GHK-Cu

Copper peptide adds collagen synthesis, ECM remodeling, and skin/connective tissue repair on top of the angiogenic healing provided by BPC-157 + TB-500. The canonical advanced healing trio is BPC-157 (local angiogenesis), TB-500 (systemic migration), and GHK-Cu (collagen quality).
SQ or topical, daily, alongside Wolverine Stack injection
KPV

Potent anti-inflammatory tripeptide (α-MSH fragment). Reduces systemic inflammation that can impede healing. Stacked to address the inflammatory component while BPC-157 and TB-500 handle structural repair.
SQ daily or oral

GHRH analogue increases IGF-1 signaling, supporting satellite cell repair and muscle protein synthesis alongside the structural healing from the Wolverine Stack. Commonly combined as the "complete recovery stack."
Evening SQ injection, separate from Wolverine Stack
Ipamorelin

Selective GH secretagogue from the GHRP-1 compound series (PMID 9849822), paired with CJC-1295 for pulsatile GH release and IGF-1 support. Adds anabolic recovery signaling to complement the Wolverine Stack healing mechanisms.
Evening SQ injection paired with CJC-1295
Avoid
Anti-VEGF therapies (bevacizumab, ranibizumab)

Directly opposes the angiogenic mechanism of both BPC-157 (VEGFR2 upregulation) and TB-500 (angiogenesis in rat studies of thymosin beta-4). Combining nullifies both peptide effects and may produce unpredictable vascular signaling.
SSRIs / SNRIs (sertraline, fluoxetine, venlafaxine)

In rats, BPC-157 interacts with dopamine and adrenergic systems (PMID 9073154) and shifts brain serotonin synthesis (PMID 15531385). Multiple community reports of worsened anxiety and panic attacks when combining BPC-157 with antidepressants. No human interaction study exists but mechanism is plausible. Discuss with prescriber.
Anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin, DOACs)
Both BPC-157 and TB-500 promote angiogenesis, which may increase bleeding risk at healing sites. The combination amplifies this concern vs. either peptide alone.
Immunosuppressants (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, mycophenolate)

TB-500 modulates immune cell migration; BPC-157 modulates leukocyte recruitment. Combined effect on immunosuppressive therapy is unknown. Theoretical risk of undermining therapeutic immunosuppression.
Compounded

FDA's Category 2 page (current as of April 22, 2026) lists BPC-157 and TB-500 as withdrawn by their nominators. PCAC discussed both on July 23, 2026. No 503A bulks rule has issued, so compounding pharmacies cannot use either today.
Pricing updated 2026-04-09

The most serious safety concern with the Wolverine Stack is its pro-angiogenic load. Both BPC-157 and TB-500 promote new blood vessel formation through different receptor pathways. In someone with an undiagnosed or subclinical tumor, that combined vascularization signal could theoretically support cancer growth. No human oncogenic data exists for either peptide, but the mechanism is real. Cancer screening before starting any cycle is not optional. Anxiety and panic attacks affect a subset of users. In rats, BPC-157 interacts with dopamine and adrenergic systems (Sikiric et al.) [4] and shifts brain serotonin synthesis [9]. Multiple community reports describe worsened anxiety when combining BPC-157 with SSRIs or SNRIs. Users on antidepressants should discuss this with their prescriber before starting. If anxiety occurs, reducing to 250 mcg total per day or discontinuing the BPC-157 component specifically is the standard community approach. The TB-500 component alone does not trigger this effect. Heart palpitations are transient and most common in the first few days. They typically resolve without intervention. Nausea is the most frequently reported side effect overall. The BPC-157 component increases gastric motility, and higher doses make it worse. Injecting before bed rather than morning helps for most users. If nausea persists past week 2, suspect product quality; mannitol filler and residual acetonitrile from HPLC purification are common culprits in research-grade vials. "Peptide flu" hits some users in weeks one and two: malaise, chills, transient fatigue. This usually resolves by week three. Headaches during loading are attributed to vasodilation from the combined angiogenic response. Injection site reactions (redness, lumps, nodules) are often caused by benzyl alcohol in bacteriostatic water rather than the peptides themselves. Switching to preservative-free sterile water reduces reactions but shortens reconstituted shelf life. Any lump larger than 1 cm persisting beyond week two warrants medical evaluation. Human safety data is extremely limited. Total published human evidence for the combination is 4 patients in one retrospective report (Lee and Padgett 2021) [7]. TB-500 itself has no published human safety data; FDA found none by any route. Two phase 1 trials, Ruff 2010 [8] and Wang 2021 [3], gave intravenous full-length thymosin beta-4 instead. BPC-157 has no completed human safety trial. Third-party testing has found inconsistent purity and labeling among research-grade peptide products. Pre-mixed blends face additional risk: if either component is compromised, the entire vial is affected. Contraindications: active cancer or cancer history, pregnancy or breastfeeding, active systemic infections, and known hypersensitivity to BPC-157, thymosin beta-4, or formulation components. When to stop: fever above 100.4 degrees F, rash, hives, worsening palpitations, severe anxiety, any sign of infection spreading. Do not push through these symptoms.
Common Issues & Solutions

Nausea within 30–60 minutes of injection: usually BPC-157-mediated gastric motility effect. Reduce dose by 50%; try injecting before bed rather than morning. If persists, rule out impure product (mannitol filler, residual acetonitrile from HPLC).

No effect after 3 weeks at 500 mcg/day: suspect product quality first: research-grade products have a high failure rate (68% mislabeled per 2025 purity audit). Verify COA (LC-MS preferred over HPLC alone). Second possibility: injury type not responsive: nerve injuries and cartilage respond slower or less reliably than tendon/ligament.
Anxiety or panic attacks: reduce dose to 250 mcg/day total; if still occurring, discontinue BPC-157 component. Users on SSRIs/SNRIs have higher risk. The TB-500 component alone does not cause this.

Pre-mixed vial dosing math: 10mg vial + 2mL BAC water = 5,000 mcg/mL total (2,500 mcg/mL each component). 5 units on U-100 syringe = 250 mcg total. 10 units = 500 mcg total. 20 units = 1,000 mcg total.

Injection site lumps or nodules: usually caused by benzyl alcohol in bacteriostatic water or improper injection depth. Rotate sites more aggressively. Switch to preservative-free sterile water if persistent (shorter shelf life but fewer reactions). Aspirate any lump >1cm that appears after week 2: deeper investigation warranted.

Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500): Product Quality high risk

Neither BPC-157 nor TB-500 is on the 503A bulks list, so licensed pharmacies cannot compound them today. All available product is an unregulated research chemical. A 2025 purity audit found 68% of peptide products mislabeled or containing impurities (Finnrick Analytics, 450 samples, 64 companies). Pre-mixed blends face additional quality risk: if either component is contaminated or misdosed, the entire vial is compromised. No FDA-regulated compounded product exists, and FDA has proposed no rule adding either to the 503A bulks list.
Require both HPLC and LC-MS/MS certificates of analysis: HPLC alone cannot distinguish closely related impurities in peptide blends
Look for mass spec confirmation that both BPC-157 (MW 1419.5 Da) and TB-500 (MW 889.0 Da) are present at the correct masses
Third-party testing preferred over an in-house COA: send a sample to Janoshik or Quality Peptides Testing if in doubt
Check for mannitol filler ratio: some products contain excessive filler, effectively under-dosing active peptide
Pre-mixed vials degrade faster than single-component vials: check reconstitution date and use within 3–4 weeks once reconstituted
A batch-specific COA ties a test result to one lot number; a generic COA without a lot number says little about the vial in hand

BPC-157 and TB-500 were both on the FDA Category 2 bulk drug substance list until their nominators withdrew them; FDA's Category 2 page (current as of April 22, 2026) lists both as withdrawn. Licensed U.S. compounding pharmacies cannot produce either component or the pre-mixed blend today. PCAC discussed both on July 23, 2026, and no FDA rule has added either to the 503A bulks list. All currently available Wolverine Stack product is an unregulated research chemical. It is sold labeled "for research purposes only" and is not approved for human use by the FDA or any regulatory agency. WADA's 2026 Prohibited List bans both components in and out of competition. BPC-157 is named under S0 (non-approved substances); TB-500 is named under S2.3 (thymosin-β4 and its derivatives). Athletes subject to anti-doping testing should not use this product. This content is for informational and research purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before using any peptide product.

faqs.a: BPC-157 drives local angiogenesis and growth factor expression at the injury site. TB-500 promotes systemic actin regulation and cell migration across larger tissue areas. The combination addresses both local and systemic repair pathways simultaneously. Community reports from hundreds of users describe faster recovery timelines with the stack compared to either peptide alone. The only controlled test, a 2026 rat Achilles study (PMID 42542926), found no added benefit over either peptide alone.

faqs.q: What is the recommended Wolverine Stack dosage?
faqs.a: Beginner: 250 mcg BPC-157 plus 250 mcg TB-500, once daily. Moderate: 500 mcg of each. Aggressive: the same 500 mcg of each, 1,000 mcg total, because 1,000 mcg a day is the community ceiling. These are community figures; no published source sets a dose for the blend. The pre-mixed vial always gives equal amounts, so any other split needs separate vials. Some protocols dose TB-500 separately 2-3x per week while running BPC-157 daily.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of the Wolverine Stack?
faqs.a: BPC-157 has limited formal human safety data; TB-500 has none. Community-reported side effects include temporary brain fog, mild lethargy during the first week, nausea, and occasional headaches. These typically resolve by day 5-7. Injection site soreness is common when dosing both peptides in the same session.

faqs.q: How long should you run the Wolverine Stack?
faqs.a: Standard community protocol is 6 weeks on, 2 weeks off. Most soft tissue injury reports describe noticeable improvement by weeks 2-3. A second 6-week cycle is common for more serious injuries. The off-period allows assessment of healing progress and reduces theoretical receptor desensitization risk.

faqs.q: Can you still get BPC-157 and TB-500?
faqs.a: Both BPC-157 and TB-500 are off the FDA Category 2 list, and FDA's Category 2 page (current as of April 22, 2026) lists them as withdrawn by their nominators. PCAC discussed both on July 23, 2026. No FDA rule has added them to the 503A bulks list, so compounding pharmacies cannot use them today. Research-grade products sold online are not FDA-reviewed for identity, purity, or sterility.

faqs.q: How do you reconstitute Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500)?
faqs.a: Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500) typically comes in 10mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500)?
faqs.a: The half-life of Wolverine Stack (BPC-157 + TB-500) is ~4-6 hours. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: (5 mg) in a single vial. BPC-157 targets local tissue repair through angiogenesis and receptor upregulation. TB-500 handles the systemic side, driving cell migration and reducing inflammation body-wide. Formal clinical trials on the blend itself don't exist yet.
